chief_complaint: sudden excruciating testicular pain, high-riding testis
hpi_details: A 29-year-old male presents with sudden-onset excruciating testicular pain that began 3 hours ago, with a high-riding testis noted on exam.
ideas: He thinks he must have severely torn a tendon or pulled a groin muscle when turning awkwardly in bed.
concerns: He is terrified that his testicle is dying from a lack of blood flow and will have to be surgically removed.
expectations: He hopes for immediate IV pain relief and an urgent scan to save his testicle before it is too late.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Testicular Torsion is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes proceeding directly to emergent surgical exploration for a classic presentation without delaying for imaging, since testicular salvage is time-critical, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: sudden excruciating testicular pain, high-riding testis
Key HPI features: A 29-year-old male presents with sudden-onset excruciating testicular pain that began 3 hours ago, with a high-riding testis noted on exam.

Objective/Exam findings: Afebrile, possible mild tachycardia from pain. Affected testis is high-riding, horizontally oriented, and exquisitely tender to palpation. Absent cremasteric reflex on the affected side. Negative Prehn sign. No inguinal hernia on exam.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Testicular Torsion.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Acute epididymitis without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Absent cremasteric reflex.
management_principles: For a classic clinical presentation (sudden severe pain, high-riding testis, absent cremasteric reflex), proceed directly to emergent surgical exploration without delaying for Doppler ultrasound; testicular salvage is time-critical
Reserve Doppler ultrasound for equivocal presentations only, and never let imaging delay definitive surgical treatment when clinical suspicion is high
Obtain immediate urologic consultation for emergent surgical detorsion and bilateral orchiopexy
Perform orchiectomy if the testis is found non-viable at exploration.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: A 29-year-old male presents with sudden-onset excruciating testicular pain that began 3 hours ago, with a high-riding testis noted on exam.
reference_soap.objective: Afebrile, possible mild tachycardia from pain. Affected testis is high-riding, horizontally oriented, and exquisitely tender to palpation. Absent cremasteric reflex on the affected side. Negative Prehn sign. No inguinal hernia on exam.
reference_soap.assessment: Classic presentation of acute testicular torsion (sudden severe pain, high-riding testis, absent cremasteric reflex); this is a surgical emergency.
reference_soap.plan: This is a surgical emergency: with a classic clinical presentation, proceed directly to emergent surgical exploration and detorsion without delaying for imaging, since testicular salvage is time-critical (ideally within 6 hours of symptom onset). Obtain immediate urologic consultation. Reserve Doppler ultrasound only for equivocal presentations, and never let imaging delay definitive surgical treatment. At surgery, perform detorsion and bilateral orchiopexy, with orchiectomy if the testis is non-viable.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Acute Testicular Torsion
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Acute Testicular Torsion
Implement evidence-based management: proceed to emergent surgical exploration for classic presentations without delaying for imaging, reserving Doppler ultrasound for equivocal cases

teaching.one_liner: Surgical emergency caused by twisting of the spermatic cord, producing acute testicular ischemia.

must_ask.say: Did this severe pain in your scrotum start suddenly, waking you up or while resting?
Along with the testicular pain, have you vomited or felt sick to your stomach?
Does gently lifting your scrotum ease the pain, or does it stay severe?
Did you suffer any hit or trauma to your groin area before the pain started?
Do you have a fever or burning when you urinate?

history.answer: Doctor, my left testicle suddenly started hurting terribly about three hours ago, and the pain is completely unbearable.
It started completely out of nowhere about three hours ago while I was just sitting at home watching television.
The pain is centered right in my left testicle, and that side looks pulled up higher than the right.
It is an excruciating, sharp, twisting pain, easily a nine or ten out of ten in severity.
The pain shoots upward into my left groin and the lower left part of my belly.
I tried gently lifting and supporting my scrotum with my hand, but it did not relieve the pain at all and actually felt worse.
No, I have never experienced any sudden pain like this before in my life.
I feel really sick to my stomach from the intense pain, and I threw up once right before coming here.
The left side looks a little puffy, and changing between standing and lying down does not change the size or relieve the pain.
No, it is not a heavy, dragging, or dull ache; it is a sharp, agonizing pain.
No, I have never felt any painless, hard lump or bump in either testicle.
No fever, no burning when I urinate, no need to pee often, and no discharge from my penis.
The skin on the left side is slightly red, but there are no black spots, blisters, or foul odor.
No, I did not get kicked or injured down there, and I was not exercising or having sex when it began.
No, I have never had mumps, and I have not had any swelling or pain in my cheeks or jaw.
Both testicles have always been down in the scrotum since I was a baby, and I have never had any groin surgeries.
No, I have not lost weight, my back does not hurt, I have no cough, and my chest has not enlarged.
I have been in a committed relationship with my girlfriend for two years, and we consistently use condoms.
No, I have never had a urinary catheter, a camera put into my bladder, or any prostate treatment.
We have not tried having children yet, and I do not have diabetes or any immune system issues.
I have always been healthy and have no chronic medical conditions.
I have never had any surgeries or hospital admissions.
I do not take any prescription medications, over-the-counter painkillers, or herbal supplements.
I have no allergies to any medications, foods, or materials like latex.
I do not smoke and have never used any tobacco or vaping products.
I only drink socially, having one or two beers with friends on occasional weekends.
I work as an accountant in an office and live in an apartment with my girlfriend.
My parents and sister are all healthy, and there is no family history of testicular or urological problems.
I thought maybe I tore a tendon or severely pulled something down there when I twisted in bed.
I'm terrified that it's losing blood and they're going to have to cut my testicle off.
I just need an immediate shot for this unbearable pain and an urgent ultrasound to see if it can be saved.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 130/82 mmHg, heart rate 98 beats/min, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, temperature 36.8°C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Patient appears in acute distress, pale, sweating, and writhing uncomfortably from severe pain.
Abdomen is soft and non-distended with mild referred tenderness in the left lower quadrant, but no guarding, rigidity, or rebound tenderness.

Left testis is high-riding, horizontally oriented, and exquisitely tender to touch, with an absent left cremasteric reflex, negative Prehn sign, and negative transillumination; right testis and scrotum are normal.
No inguinal bulge, cough impulse, or hernia palpable bilaterally, and no inguinal lymphadenopathy.
